answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can tie each identity to a vault that locks a small refundable stake, so spinning up thousands of fake agents costs real money. A falcon-style reputation check then watches how agents actually behave over time instead of trusting a fresh account, and a relic of past work, like signed attestations from earlier trades, stays attached to the identity so a new clone starts with nothing. Faking all three at scale gets expensive fast.
